html:
The Malagasy are the people of Madagascar, whose language and culture join Southeast Asian and East African roots. The map uses the name for the island's people in its 800 and 900 snapshots.

Their language belongs to the Austronesian family and is closest to Ma'anyan, spoken in southern Borneo. Settlers from island Southeast Asia crossed the Indian Ocean roughly in the middle of the first millennium, and Bantu-speaking people from the East African coast came too. Genetic studies find both ancestries in nearly every Malagasy today.

Around 800 and 900, villages of rice farmers and cattle herders were spreading inland from the coasts, and the north traded with Swahili and Arab merchants. Earlier peoples remembered in legend as the Vazimba were absorbed. Kingdoms such as Merina came many centuries later.
